stories.headline: Panicked Evacuations Mix With Nonchalance in Hurricane Sandy’s Path
stories.summary: In New York City, with memories of last year’s less-than-ferocious Hurricane Irene still fresh, some skeptical residents simply would not move.

stories.headline: Voters Give Romney Better Grades for Leadership, Polls in 3 States Find
stories.summary: Mitt Romney is seen by more voters as a strong leader after his debate performance last week, but positive economic news appears to have buffered President Obama.

stories.headline: Suspect in Libya Attack, in Plain Sight, Scoffs at U.S.
stories.summary: Days after President Obama vowed to apprehend those behind the attack on American diplomats, a suspected ringleader spent an evening at a luxury hotel full of journalists.

stories.headline: Utah Mayor Hopes Star Turn, and Romney’s Star Power, Lift Her to the House
stories.summary: Mia Love would be the first black Republican woman in the House, but she says the only history she wants to make is “getting our country on track.”

stories.headline: GORBACHEV, LAST SOVIET LEADER, RESIGNS; U.S. RECOGNIZES REPUBLICS' INDEPENDENCE
stories.summary: Mikhail S. Gorbachev, the trailblazer of the Soviet Union's retreat from the cold war and the spark for the democratic reforms that ended 70 years of Communist tyranny, told a weary, anxious nation tonight that he was resigning as President and closing out the union. "I hereby discontinue my activities at the post of President of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics," declared the 60-year-old politician, the last leader of a totalitarian empire that was undone across the six years and nine months of his stewardship.

stories.headline: For Needy Children, Caring Hearts
stories.summary: This time of year, many people are digging deeper to pay for gifts to make their childrens' day brighter. The charities affiliated with The New York Times Neediest Cases Fund are digging deeper to brighten the lives of children year-round. The donations the Fund receives translates into many kinds of help. For a 3 1/2-year-old boy infected with H.I.V., a program financed by fund provides counseling to deal with the heartbreak. For a group of 10-year-olds, a volunteer's dedication has created a newspaper in which they chronicle their lives Articles, page 48.

stories.headline: AFTER THE SOVIET UNION: Capitalism's New Frontier - A special report; Hunting for Riches in Ex-Soviet Lands
stories.summary: American companies are treating the territories of the now-defunct Soviet Union as wild, unpredictable places, without reliable laws, but good for trying to strike it rich with ventures that skim the cream from an economy in disarray. Even Fortune 500 companies are signing deals that have a frontier quality. In fact, the upheaval seems to be stimulating imaginative deal-making, not inhibiting it. The greater the turmoil and risk, the greater the concessions the authorities in the newly independent lands seem willing to grant, although concern is surfacing that deals born today may be canceled tomorrow by some future government that views them as one-sided and exploitative. Promise of Big Profits The guiding principle appears to be this: Gamble as little as possible in a risky investment that might very well return a jackpot profit, if the money is not lost altogether in the chaos. Robert S. Strauss, a millionaire Texas lawyer and the United States Ambassador to Moscow, describes the potential and the risk by advising business people that if he were younger -- he is 73 -- he would invest $100,000 in the old Soviet Union and run it up into $10 million, but that if he had $10 million, he would gamble only $100,000 of it.

stories.headline: Recalling Pearl Harbor, Bush Urges an End to Rancor; 50 Years After Attack, Survivors Are Told to Forget Animosity
stories.summary: Amid solemn ceremonies honoring the Americans who died in the Japanese surprise attack on Pearl Harbor 50 years ago today, President Bush told an assemblage of more than 2,000 survivors that the time had come to put aside their animosity toward Japan. "I have no rancor in my heart toward Germany or Japan -- none at all," said the President, a former Navy pilot who was himself shot down by the Japanese in the Pacific in. "I hope you have none in yours. This is no time for recrimination."

stories.headline: 2nd Bombing Suspect Caught After Frenzied Hunt Paralyzes Boston
stories.summary: The teenage suspect in the Boston Marathon bombings, Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev, was taken into custody in Watertown, Mass., after a search that left his brother dead and the Boston area virtually shut down.

stories.headline: From Wrinkles to Rap, a Rock Award’s Shifting Cast
stories.summary: Randy Newman, Public Enemy and Quincy Jones were among the honorees Thursday night at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame’s induction ceremony in Los Angeles.

stories.headline: In Gun Bill Defeat, a President’s Distaste for Twisting Arms
stories.summary: The White House defended President Obama’s efforts on gun violence, but he has long struggled to master his relationship with Congress.

stories.headline: Same Story, Different Screens: A Video Game That’s Also a Series
stories.summary: The video game Defiance and the television series of the same title were created in a collaboration between the Syfy network and Trion Worlds, a gaming company.
